<!--
========================================================================
HOW TO USE THIS FILE
========================================================================
This is a TARGET, not a draft. It is the linear results paper the
pre-registration (05_paper.qmd) is scaffolding for. The pre-reg reads
like a legal brief because it must pre-litigate every objection BEFORE
the data. The results paper carries none of that burden. Three moves
shed ~a third to half the pre-reg's text:

  1. DROP the branching. The contingency tree, "if the diagonal doesn't
     hold", persistence-vs-collapse, calibration pass/fail, the tau
     sweep — all branch on unknowns. The results paper walks ONE
     realized branch. Report the path taken; drop the other three.

  2. RESULTS not PROMISES. "X is predicted to fall below independence,
     and here is the elaborate reason that is the right test" becomes
     "X falls below independence (Table N)." The justification for the
     test compresses to a sentence because the reader sees it worked.

  3. RELOCATE the defenses. Confound discharges (forward-drift,
     selection-symmetry, differential-contamination) move to a lean
     Limitations section AND to the pre-reg-as-appendix-of-record. Do
     NOT delete them — CITE them. The pre-registration is your answer
     to the "went in with a knife" referee; the results paper must
     POINT BACK to it. The slog becomes the record the clean paper
     leans on.

RULE OF THUMB per section below:
  [KEEP]      survives largely intact
  [COMPRESS]  N paragraphs -> N sentences once it's a result
  [RELOCATE]  moves to Limitations or cites the pre-reg
  [DROP]      pre-reg-only scaffolding the results retire
  [NEW]       the actual results — the only genuinely new writing
========================================================================
-->
